design_system_examples.overview: Complete workflow examples demonstrating how to use the UX Designer mode to create design systems, components, and improve user experience in Next.js applications.

workflow.name: creating_design_system_from_scratch
workflow.description: Complete example of setting up a design system for a new Next.js project with Tailwind CSS, including configuration, tokens, and base components.

scenario.context: Starting with a fresh Next.js project that has basic Tailwind setup. Goal is to create a cohesive design system for a SaaS application.

step.title: Analyze Current State
step.action: Use codebase_search to understand existing setup

step.title: Configure Design Tokens
step.action: Update Tailwind configuration with design system tokens

step.title: Setup Global Styles and Typography
step.action: Create comprehensive global styles with proper font loading

step.title: Create Utility Functions
step.action: Setup utility functions for class merging and component variants

step.title: Create Base Button Component
step.action: Implement accessible button component with multiple variants

step.title: Test and Validate Design System
step.action: Use browser tools to test the implementation

testing_steps.test: Create a test page with all button variants
Test responsive behavior at different screen sizes

expected_outcomes.outcome: Consistent design tokens available throughout the application
Accessible button component with multiple variants
Proper font loading and typography hierarchy

scenario.name: color_palette_migration
scenario.description: Migrating from hardcoded colors to design system tokens

replacement_strategy.step: Search for hardcoded color usage across components
Map existing colors to semantic design tokens
Replace with consistent design system colors
Test visual consistency across all components

scenario.name: spacing_consistency
scenario.description: Standardizing spacing patterns across the application

replacement_strategy.step: Map to Tailwind's standard spacing scale

audit_checklist.check: Color contrast ratios meet WCAG standards
All images have descriptive alt text
Focus indicators are visible and consistent

test_case.name: button_component_testing
test_case.description: Comprehensive testing approach for button component

visual_tests.test: All variants render with correct styles

responsive_tests.test: Touch targets are adequate on mobile (44px minimum)
Text remains readable at all sizes
Buttons stack properly on narrow screens

breakpoint_tests.test: Content remains accessible at all sizes
Navigation works on mobile and desktop

performance_tests.test: Layout shift is minimal during load

symptoms.symptom: Tailwind classes don't seem to take effect
Custom components don't show expected styling

debugging_steps.step: Check Tailwind config content paths include all template files
Verify classes are not being purged incorrectly
Use browser dev tools to inspect actual applied styles
Ensure Tailwind directives are imported in globals.css

symptoms.symptom: Responsive classes don't activate at expected breakpoints

debugging_steps.step: Verify viewport meta tag is present in layout
Check breakpoint syntax (sm:, md:, lg:, etc.)
Test with browser dev tools responsive mode
Check for conflicting CSS that overrides Tailwind
Use browser accessibility dev tools to audit
Test with actual screen reader software
